Property management.text: Our Real Estate property management revenue arrangements consist of providing operational and administrative services to manage a subject property. Fees for these services are typically billed and collected monthly. Property management service fees are recognized as revenue over time using the output method as the performance obligations under the customer arrangement are satisfied each month. Our Real Estate title insurance commission fee revenue is earned when the sale of the title insurance is completed, which corresponds to the point in time when the underlying real estate sale transaction closes and the payment is received.

Property management.text: Our Real Estate property management revenue arrangements consist of providing operational and administrative services to manage a subject property. Fees for these services are typically billed and collected monthly. Property management service fees are recognized as revenue over time using the output method as the performance obligations under the customer arrangement are satisfied each month. Our Real Estate title insurance commission fee revenue is earned when the sale of the title insurance is completed, which corresponds to the point in time when the underlying real estate sale transaction closes and the payment is received.

gp.text: Gross profit. We define gross profit as the remaining portion after real estate agent commissions are subtracted from our revenues. Gross profit was $261,084 for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $251,808 for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $9,276 (4%). This increase primarily resulted from increased existing home sales in our Northeast region as well as our Development Marketing division, in which sales of developer-represented units for the year ended December 31, 2025 contributed to an increase in gross profit.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our business significantly depends on sales transactions for residential property in t he New York metropolitan area, and we derived approximate ly 50% of our revenues in 2025, 49% of our revenues in 2024 and 51% of our revenues i n 2023 from the New York metropolitan area.
• We depend on a strong brand, and any failure to maintain, protect and enhance the Douglas Elliman brand would have an adverse effect on our ability to grow our real estate brokerage business;
• Our real estate brokerage business depends on the success of our agents;

• We rely on licenses to use the intellectual property rights of third parties which are incorporated into our products and services, and failure to renew or expand existing licenses may require us to modify, limit or discontinue certain offerings;
• If websites we rely on fail to rank prominently in unpaid search results, traffic to these websites could decline and our business would be adversely affected;
• Douglas Elliman Inc. is a holding company and depends on cash payments from our subsidiaries to meet our obligations;
The real estate market also depends upon the strength of financial institutions, which are sensitive to changes in the general macroeconomic environment.
The success of our business depends on the ability of our brokers and agents to sell homes.
Accordingly, our financial results depend upon the operational and financial success of our brokerage offices and our agents.
Our business model depends upon our agents’ success in generating gross commission income, which we collect and from which we pay to them net commissions.
Our operations rely on the performance of real estate agents.
Our ability to attract agents and appeal to clients depends upon providing and maintaining a robust number of listings.
We rely on a combination of protections provided by contracts, as well as copyright, trademark, and other laws, to protect our intellectual property from infringement, misappropriation or dilution.
We rely on licenses to use the intellectual property rights of third parties which are incorporated into our products and services.
We rely on products, technologies and intellectual property that we license from third parties for use in our services.
We rely on traffic to our websites, including our flagship website, elliman.com, directed from search engines.
Additionally, we increasingly rely on third-party providers, including cloud storage solution providers.
As a result, you should not rely upon our historical results of operations as indicators of future performance.
Douglas Elliman Inc. is a holding company and depends on cash payments from our subsidiaries to meet our cash obligations.
In addition to our own cash resources, our ability to meet our cash obligations depends on the ability of our subsidiaries to make cash available to us.

Accordingly, if no such future dividends are declared, you must rely on sales of your common stock after price appreciation, which may never occur, as the only way to realize any positive return on your investment in our common stock.

Our decision to issue securities in any future offering will depend on market conditions and other factors beyond our control, which may adversely affect the amount, timing or nature of our future offerings.

The amount of the annual limitation depends upon the value of the Company immediately before the change, changes to the Company's capital during a specified period prior to the change, and the federal published interest rate.
